newsitem.title: USA: US stocks appear fully valued - NY Fed's McDonough.
newsitem.headline: US stocks appear fully valued - NY Fed's McDonough.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President William McDonough said he thought U.S. stocks appear fully valued but he was not sure if they were overvalued.
Speaking at a breakfast sponsored by the New York City Partnership, McDonough said, "I have no idea," when asked if he thought the stock market was overvalued.
"Does it seem to be rather fully valued?," McDonough asked. "By all conventional measures, yes," he said.
McDonough reiterated that he doesn't know what the proper valuation of this or any other stock market is. "The real truth is, nobody else does either."
He said the free market working sets a price and those prices are "usually reasonably rational."
McDonough said Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's "irrational exuberance" remark was not a statement, rather he was asking a question.
"I believe that was pulled out of context and the implication was that he made a statement," McDonough said.
"He asked a question -- a very rational question," he said.

When asked about the current levels of exchange rates, McDonough said "I think that there are many market analysts who would say the present level of exchange rates is pretty close to economic fundamentals."
In addition, McDonough said oil prices are a matter of great interest to the Fed.
McDonough said when he looks at price stability, he tends to look at core inflation, which leaves out food and energy prices.
"Although I don't think we could use energy prices as a guide for monetary policy, oil prices are a matter of concern to us," he said.
